x: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 rests on Article 253, which lets Parliament make laws to carry out international agreements, here the 1972 Stockholm decisions. Articles 48A and 51A(g) are directives and duties.
t: Discriminate the law-making Article from the directive Articles.

x: Option C is incorrect: the NGT was set up on 18 October 2010 under the NGT Act, 2010, for speedy disposal of environmental cases.
t: Recall the NGT date.

x: Both are true: Article 48A directs the State to protect the environment, forests and wildlife, and the 42nd Amendment (1976) added it. When it was added does not explain what it says, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a history explains a content.

x: GEAC deals with genetically engineered organisms, CGWA was set up under Section 3(3) of the EPA, the NGT under the NGT Act, 2010, and the CPCB under the Water Act, 1974. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Match each body to its legal basis.

x: All four are correct: Section 3(3) lets the Centre create authorities, Section 5 covers directions, Section 15 sets penalties, and the Jan Vishwas Act, 2023 replaced jail terms with monetary penalties for many contraventions.
t: Recall the key EPA sections.
s:
Consider the following statements about the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986: I. Section 3(3) provides the power to constitute authorities. II. Section 5 deals with directions and measures. III. Section 15 deals with penalties for contravention of the Act. IV. The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2023 replaced imprisonment with monetary penalties for many contraventions under the Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Both are true: the EPA aims to protect and improve the environment, and it gives the Centre a coordinating role. The Centre's role is a means, not the purpose, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a means explains a purpose.

x: All three are correct: Article 51A(g) asks citizens to protect and improve the natural environment and to have compassion for living creatures.
t: Recall the duty in Article 51A(g).
s:
Consider the following statements about Article 51A(g):
I. It directs citizens to protect the natural environment.
II. It directs citizens to improve the natural environment.
III. It directs citizens to show compassion for living creatures.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: All three are correct: GEAC was set up under the EPA, was once the Genetic Engineering Approval Committee, and was renamed 'Appraisal' in 2010.
t: Recall GEAC's renaming.
s:
Consider the following statements about the Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee:
I. It was constituted under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
II. Its earlier name was the Genetic Engineering Approval Committee.
III. The Genetic Engineering Approval Committee was renamed the Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee in 2010.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Both are true: the Central Ground Water Authority regulates both the development and the management of groundwater.
t: Recall the CGWA's role.

x: All five are linked with the NGT: environmental matters, forests and natural resources, a basis in Article 21, and the right to a healthy environment.
t: Recall the NGT's scope.

x: The CPCB abates water pollution, improves air quality, and promotes clean streams and wells. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
t: Match each function to its object.

x: The EPA is called umbrella legislation, the Bhopal gas tragedy (1984) was its background, and the Stockholm Conference (1972) was its source. The answer is (a)-(iii), (b)-(ii), (c)-(i).
t: Match each item to its detail.

x: Option C is incorrect: NEERI in Nagpur, earlier CPHERI and set up in 1958, is a CSIR laboratory, not part of the NGT.
t: Match NEERI to its parent body.

x: Both are true: activities in eco-sensitive zones are regulated rather than banned because these zones are buffers meant to protect nearby sensitive areas. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the purpose explains the rule.

x: NEERI (Nagpur, CSIR) works on environmental science and engineering. Clearances, tribunals and forest diversion belong to other bodies.
t: Recall NEERI's focus.

x: Both are true: the EPA, 1986, is umbrella legislation, and the NGT Act, 2010, is about environmental justice.
t: Recall the role of each law.

x: The Wildlife Act covers wildlife, the Water Act water pollution, and the Air Act air pollution. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-i.
t: Match each Act to its subject.

x: Eco-sensitive zones are notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, around protected areas.
t: Recall the law behind eco-sensitive zones.

x: All three are correct: the NEAA was set up under its 1997 Act, no longer exists, and its role passed to the NGT.
t: Recall what happened to the NEAA.

x: Option B is incorrect: the NGT's constitutional basis is Article 21 (the right to life, read to include a healthy environment), not Article 28. Justice Lokeshwar Singh Panta was its first chair.
t: Recall the NGT's constitutional basis.

x: Both are true: the CPCB is a statutory body under the Water Act, 1974, and it promotes clean streams and wells. A function does not explain a legal status, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a function explains a status.

x: NGT is the National Green Tribunal, Justice L.S. Panta was its first chair, the CPCB is a statutory body under the Water Act, and the NEAA came from its 1997 Act. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv.
t: Match each item to its detail.

x: I and II are correct: the NGT was set up on 18 October 2010 to deliver environmental justice. III is false because improving air quality is the CPCB's job.
t: Discriminate the NGT from the CPCB.

x: All four are correct: the NGT hears cases on forest conservation, natural resources and the environment.
t: Recall the NGT's scope.

x: The National Environment Appellate Authority was dissolved after the NGT took over its work.
t: Recall what the NGT replaced.

x: By hearing environmental cases itself, the NGT reduces the load on the High Courts and Supreme Court. Clean streams and air quality are CPCB functions.
t: Discriminate the NGT from the CPCB.

x: The Wildlife Act (1972) covers wildlife, the Water Act (1974) water pollution, the Forest Conservation Act (1980) forests, and the Air Act (1981) air pollution. The answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Match each subject to its Act.

x: Option C is incorrect: R2 is a code for responsible electronics recycling. EIA is the process of assessing a project's likely environmental impact before it starts.
t: Discriminate R2 from EIA.

x: Both are true: the Water Act, 1974, created the CPCB, and the right to a healthy environment is linked with Article 21 and the NGT.
t: Recall the CPCB and NGT links.

x: The Biological Diversity Act, 2002, covers biodiversity and access and benefit sharing, following the CBD.
t: Match each Act to its subject.

x: The EPA dates from 1986, the Biological Diversity Act 2002, the Forest Rights Act 2006, and the NGT Act 2010. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Arrange the Acts in time order.

x: Both are true: the EPA is an umbrella law because it covers the environment as a whole, not one part of it. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the scope explains the 'umbrella' label.

x: The Forest Rights Act centres on forest-dwelling communities, the NGT Act on environmental justice, forest-dweller rights come from the FRA (2006), and the tribunal law is the NGT Act (2010). The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Match each item to its detail.

x: EIA is linked with environmental clearance: a project's impacts are assessed before it is approved.
t: Recall what EIA leads to.
